newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen treading water.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.22 percent on Monday and traders forecast the blue-chip SBI index would remain hemmed into a narrow box range this week.
"The market is in waiting mode for the return of foreign investors. Until then volumes will remain low," a trader said.
"At the moment a lot depends upon the parliament's decision whether to ratify the association agreement with the European Union," said Goran Spasenic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
"If the accord is not ratified within two weeks, the market could collapse as that would scare international investors away," he added.

Parliament said it would take a vote on whether to ratify the agreement after the Constitutional Court decides whether ratification would not conflict with the constitution, which still bars foreigners from buying real estate. The court is expected to decide by June 5.
The SBI index fell 3.48 points to 1,314.99.
Issue A of drug company Lek was most actively traded, down 1.11 percent to 24,080 tolars on volume of 275 shares.

Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, down 9.88 percent to 6,930 on volume of five shares. Traders said it was difficult to forecast future moves as trading volume remained extremely thin in the brokerage's shares.
Bank UBK was the top gainer, up 6.83 percent to 6,100 on volume of 100 shares but traders pointed out that the gain in the fairly illiquid share was made in a single transaction.
